candidates.name: Cathedral
candidates.content: Huge 15th-century church on the site of the former great mosque; richly decorated with the central nave rising to 37 m. An ornate canopy and statue marks the final resting place of Christopher Columbus. If there's a queue for tick

candidates.name: Real Alcázar
candidates.content: A beautiful palace in Mudéjar (Moorish) style, built in the 12th century by the Almohad Caliphs. Greatly remodelled and extended in the 14th century by Pedro I the Cruel, its myriad rooms, extravagant architecture, lavish gardens

candidates.name: Palacio de Las Dueñas
candidates.price: Fee: €10 with audio guide, ask for reduced prices
candidates.content: Las Dueñas is a palace belonging to the House of Alba. It was built in the 15th century, with Renaissance architecture style and Gothic-Mudejar influences. The palace is one of the major historic homes in the city. The poet Antoni

candidates.name: Palacio de la Condesa de Lebrija
candidates.alt: Palace of the Countess of Lebrija
candidates.content: The palace is considered the 'best paved house-palace in Europe' owing to its collection of Roman mosaics and marble floors in the 'opus sectile' geometric style, which paved practically the whole of the ground floor. There is als

candidates.name: Metropol Parasol
candidates.content: An enormous wooden structure, designed by German architect Jürgen Mayer-Hermann, inspired by the Cathedral of Seville and in the form of giant mushrooms. Known to locals as 'las setas' (the mushrooms), the structure covers the Cen

candidates.name: Museo de Bellas Artes
candidates.hours: 1 Sep – 31 Jul: Tue-Sat 09:00-21:00, Sun and holidays 09:00-15:00; 1-31 Aug: Tue-Sat 09:00-15:30
candidates.content: Considered by some as the second most important fine arts museum in Spain after the Prado in Madrid. The museum building is a former mercy convent renewed in the 17th century and the 15 exhibition rooms show a comprehensive pictur

candidates.name: Museo Antiquarium
candidates.content: A museum with excavated Roman and Moorish remains, discovered during construction of the Metropol Parasol. You can enter for free if you show your ticket for the alcazar, even if the ticket is a few days old.

candidates.name: Centro Andaluz de Arte Contempraneo
candidates.price: Visit monument €1.80; Temporary exhibitions €1.80; Complete Visit €3.01. Free on Tu-Fr 19:00-21:00 Sa 11:00-21:00
candidates.content: Contemporary art museum in the former Carthusian monastery of Santa Maria of Las Cuevas, which has a fascinating history as a clay mine, monastery, and ceramics factory. The site and expansive grounds are worth a visit in their ow

candidates.name: Torre del Oro
candidates.price: €3 adults, €1.50 seniors/students/children 6-14, free children under 6; €2 for audioguide
candidates.content: A 13th-century tower, the top of which is rumored to have once been covered in gold. It now houses the local maritime museum.

candidates.name: Casa de Pilatos
candidates.content: A 16th-century palace and generally thought to be one of the best in the city.

candidates.name: Museo Arqueológico de Sevilla
candidates.hours: 16 Sep – 31 May: Tue-Sat 10:00-20:30, Sun and holidays 10:00-17:00; 1 Jun – 15 Sep: Tue-Sat 09:00-15:30, Sun and holidays 10:00-17:00
candidates.content: It has one of the best collection of Roman-era artifacts in Spain, brought from nearby Italica.

candidates.name: Hospital de los Venerables
candidates.content: A 17th-century retirement home and hospital for aged and sickly retired priests, restored by the Fundación to preserve an example of Andalusian architecture at its very best. Includes a resplendent Baroque chapel which is highly r

candidates.name: Parque María Luisa
candidates.content: Built for the 1929 Iber-Americano World's Fair and now landscaped with attractive monuments and museums.

candidates.name: Palacio Arzobispal
candidates.content: It is in the historical section of the city and is home to various clergy and the Archbishop. On the outside you only can catch a glimpse of the patio but on the inside there are important works of art.

candidates.name: Archivo General de Indias
candidates.hours: Tue-Sat 09:30-17:00 (last entry: 16:30); Sun and public holidays 10:00-14:00 (last entry: 13:30); Mon closed
candidates.content: This Renaissance building houses extensive archives relating to the Spanish conquest of the Americas, and is designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Included in the collection are the diaries of Columbus. The archive hosts rotati

candidates.name: Plaza de España
candidates.content: The site of the Spanish pavilion from the 1929 exhibition: the semi-circle has little ceramic maps of every region of Spain plus images of them and/or their history. It was also used in the filming of the Star Wars prequels. Visit

candidates.name: Real Fábrica de Tabacos
candidates.hours: During term time only: Mon-Fri 10:00-20:00, Sat 10:00-14:00
candidates.content: The main building of the University of Seville was once the Tobacco Factory of Seville, and was constructed between 1728 and 1771 by Sebastián Van der Bocht. Over the main entrance, the triangular façade ends in a statue of La Fam

candidates.name: Alameda de Hercules
candidates.content: Authentic and less touristy plaza with local food opportunities.

candidates.name: Museo del Baile Flamenco
candidates.price: Museum: €10 adult, €8 senior, €6 child; performances: €20 adults, €14 senior, €12 child
candidates.content: Offers an experience for all the senses with ambiental music, videos, touch-screens and artifacts to be found in this 18th century building at the heart of the historical Barrio Santa Cruz. On Friday and Saturday evenings a specta

candidates.name: Plaza de Toros de la Real Maestranza
candidates.price: €7 adult, €4 senior or student, €3 child 7-11, free for child under 6; free on M 15:00-19:00
candidates.hours: Nov-Apr 09:30-19:00, May and Oct 09:30-20:00, Jun-Sep 09:30-23:00; on bull fighting days 09:30-15:00
candidates.content: Bullfighting is not a sport for all; those who are either squeamish or have convictions on animal welfare should stay clear, as the event concludes with the killing of the bulls. Failing that, a visit to the arena and the attached

candidates.name: Feria de Abril
candidates.content: Also known as "Feria de Sevilla" - a release after the somberness of Semana Santa. To say this is a huge party would be an understatement. Most if not all of Seville takes a week's holiday (the Wednesday of Feria week is a public

candidates.name: Semana Santa
candidates.content: The sombre Easter week processions feature thousands of people and go on all week, a spectacular display of conspicuous Catholicism.

candidates.name: La Carbonería
candidates.content: Offers free flamenco shows nightly. Arrive early for good seats.

candidates.name: La Casa del Flamenco
candidates.content: A good spot to see real flamenco.

candidates.name: Real Betis
candidates.content: Capacity 60,700. Their women's team play in Liga F (their top tier) at the nearby Luis del Sol training ground.

candidates.name: Sevilla FC
candidates.content: Capacity 42,500. Their women's team play in Liga F at Ramón Cisneros training ground 5 km southeast of the centre.

candidates.name: Parcería Café
candidates.content: Situated near Mercado Feria, Parcería is a tiny café serving coffee from a local roaster. Laptops aren’t allowed, but the coffee is worth a walk from the city centre.

candidates.name: CafeTeaTe
candidates.content: Located inside the Triana market, this café also serves breakfast sandwiches and other items. Their espresso shots are slightly longer than one might expect, but still decent. Make sure to ask about the current coffees when you or

candidates.name: Utopía Café
candidates.content: Hidden in a side street, Utopía is a takeaway-only café serving coffee from the same local roaster as Parcería.

candidates.name: Delatribu
candidates.content: A small takeaway café serving organic coffee and homemade pastry.

candidates.name: Naturalmente
candidates.content: Breakfast and lunch every day, with early dinner two nights a week - handy if you want to eat earlier than typical Spanish dining hours. The menu has a wide choice of breakfast "toasts", fruit and yoghurt bowls, cakes and pastries

candidates.name: El Librero Tapas y Quesos
candidates.content: Does cheese dishes, ham dishes, tapas, menu del dia, etc. Very popular with locals.

candidates.name: Los Coloniales
candidates.content: This tapas place is cozy and has only a few tables. Go there early to put your name on the board to get a table, then head inside for a couple of beers. Portions are large and food is very very good. Nice homemade desserts, too.

candidates.name: Duo Tapas
candidates.content: This bar offers a nice atmosphere and good food. The price is average and the size of the tapas is fair, but it may be crowded, so it's better not to go in a hurry, as you may need to wait for a table.

candidates.name: Bodeguita Romero
candidates.content: A classic neighbourhood bodega, very popular with locals and serving excellent tapas.

candidates.name: Cafe-Bar Las Teresas
candidates.content: A lively slice of ham heaven. Tourists and locals. If the sight of dead hogs hanging from the rafters offends you -- drink and eat elsewhere.

candidates.name: Restaurante Fez
candidates.content: Maroccan cuisine. Since you need a break from tapas. There are lots of other places serving Arabic food.

candidates.name: El Rinconcillo
candidates.content: The oldest tavern around, try the Espinacas con Garbanzos (spinach with chickpeas) and Salmorejo, while watching the witty bartenders running around and writing your bill on the bar in front of you with, get this, chalk.

candidates.name: Habanita
candidates.content: In the centre of the city. Quiet open air restaurant with a very good selection of vegetarian and vegan foods.

Triana offers many ceramic factories where one can buy various tiles from authentic craftsmen.
